scarface-1932_202109: Scarface (also known as Scarface: The Shame of the Nation and The Shame of a Nation ) is a 1932 American pre-Code gangster film directed by Howard Hawks and produced by Hawks and Howard Hughes . The screenplay, by Ben Hecht , is based loosely on the 1929 novel by Armitage Trail which was inspired by Al Capone . The film stars Paul Muni as Italian immigrant gangster Antonio "Tony" Camonte, a gangster who violently rises through the Chicago gangland. Meanwhile, Camonte pursues his bosses'…

rv: A classic that ran so the remake could sprint.

One of the greatest gangster movies ever made. Everything about this from the unforgettable performance of Paul Muni, to the sharp and witty dialogue and direction of good ol’ Howard Hawks, the unusually violent nature even for a film made in this particular era of Pre-Code Hollywood, the engaging and fast paced story even by today’s standards that is easy to understand and get into, and the fact that this was produced by the one and only Howard Hughes makes this an all-time favorite for me. “Get outta the way Johnny, I’m gonna spit!”

One of the many Great films directed by Howard Hawks. With the superb acting of Paul Muni as Tony Comonte the bad-ass, not to bright, devil-may-care gangster. The faithfull right hand man and henchman for Tony is played by George Raft as Rinaldo. The sweet Ann Dvorak as his sister Cesca who does a sexy little dance, that I loved., to entice Rinaldo. Boris Karloft as a gangster is even in this film ! This film produced by Howard Hughes & Hawks was also filmed with an alternate ending, it's here on Archive somewhere. 5 Stars all the way X X X X X
Louis Pasteur pops a cap on Norman Bates' dad

That's Anthony Perkins' ("Psycho") father as the weasley Lovo. And Muni won an award for Louis Pasteur. That thing Tony's got going on for his sister......lots of innuendo, a Freudian would love analyzing this movie. Re: the remake : a Cuban stereotype with a bad accent played by an Italian guy, can't even come close to an Italian stereotype with a bad accent played by a Jewish guy. There was "Little Caesar" with Edgar G. Robinson and "Public Enemy" with Cagney in 1931. And "Scarface" in '32. All the gangster movies after that are footnotes of the genre.

rv: A must see education piece if I ever saw one - for historical, anthropological, philosophical, and technical reasons

Wow.. on so many levels. Shot, apparently by HAND by Edison himself, in the aftermath of the 1906 SF earthquake. The historical value of this footage cannot be stressed. Anthropologically, to glimpse what life and lifestyle was like at the turn of the century is eye-opening. It really didn't sink in that horses were still the primary mode of transportation, and that ALL of the roads were dirt - yet the advent of the motor carriage and the motion picture camera are clearly objects of interest due to their obvious rarity.
